description.purpose: The session handover step (R-OS-3): when a session generation closes and the collector hands the day out as one write batch, this hive turns that batch into ONE fresh, recency-weighted summary - more from the last turns, phase-out before, hard facts kept - and emits it as a system.handover update, the form an llm cell consumes without a provider call. The next generation opens lazily and wakes up with yesterday instead of with nothing, so the transition is not noticeable. A glue cell shapes the prompt (the prompt lives in the glue phase, not in the llm config), a writer llm writes the prose, and a failed call leaves on its own error route instead of being swallowed. Since 2.1.0 the four weighting knobs of `./prep` are params of that cell instead of environment substitution tokens ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138)): an `override_params` entry can name them, so two summarizers in one colony weight their days apart. Since 2.2.2 ([#886](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/886)) `./writer` declares `hop.model`, the model the provider served; nothing else moved. Since 2.2.3 ([#890](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/890)) `./writer` declares every hop key the `llm` cell writes into an answer, the cache keys among them; nothing else moved. Since 2.2.4 ([#993](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/993)) `./writer` declares the optional hop key `dropped`, the sampling fields a model's `supported_params` left out; nothing else moved. Since 2.2.5 ([#999](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/999)) `./writer` declares the optional hop key `unverified`, the sampling fields sent without a `supported_params` list to check them; nothing else moved. Since 2.2.7 ([#801](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/801)) its model cell takes the provider key as a sealed vault grant (`credential_grant_id`, asked on `credential_request`, answered on `in_sealed`) instead of `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from the process environment; a literal key in the instance still works for 0.62.x while no grant is set. Where a key comes from is a repair of the promise, so it is the third digit.Since 2.2.8 ([#1085](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1085)) a turn and a tool text have no length of their own: `./prep` sends the day whole up to half of the writer's window -- the request's `input_soft`, else `input_soft_fallback`, the window of the catalog row the writer is born on -- and cuts fairly with a mark beyond it; a prompt the writer refuses as over its `input_hard` is sized once more at half of the number the refusal names.
description.use_when: One per agent, behind the collector's 'write' route. Instantiate with ctx.model (a resolved literal, K-H2) and wire the ports in the SAME mutation: the batch lane in, the summary route to wherever the handover belongs - typically the agent llm's system.handover slot - and a drain or alarm for summary_error. This hive is the ONLY writer of system.handover (R-OS-1 slot discipline).
description.not_in_scope: No session lifecycle: the keeper decides when a generation ends and the collector produces the batch - this hive only consumes it. No memory extraction: one summary is written, what else the batch is worth belongs to the memory hive the same batch can also be routed to. No retry: retry is edge business; the template emits summary_error once and the parent tree decides. No tool use in the writer, and no judgement about where the summary lands - the parent edges decide the target.
examples: PORTS - Entry (onto the hive path, the parent edge names the lane): in_batch, wired as {from: <collector>, to: <summarizer>, condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'write', modifier: {set_hop: {route: 'in_batch'}}} - it consumes exactly the collector's close-batch form (messages[] the whole day, top-level slot 'rounds', hop.session_id/turn_count/round_count). Exit (from the hive path, on hop.route): 'summary' -> one system.handover update per batch (hop.session_id, hop.summary_chars), typically to the agent llm; 'summary_error' -> the degradation lane (hop.error_code), MUST be drained by the parent.

a 40-turn day closes -> the newest 12 turns travel verbatim, the older 28 whole and counted, tool rounds as context (with context.input_soft: half of that window, cut fairly with a mark) -> one summary on route 'summary'
the provider fails with a 500 -> exactly one message on route 'summary_error' with error_code provider_error, and no half-summary behind it
an empty session closes -> the prompt says '0 turns' and the shipped instructions demand a short honest summary instead of invention

MODEL DOOR (since 2.2.0, GH #858): `in_model` takes a params-only body -- a model package the colony's llm-registry pushes -- from the hive's own path straight to `./writer`, its one llm cell, which merges it into its live params and answers nothing. `./writer` states what it needs in `params.requirement` (prose, never a model name); without a registry the door stays unused.

model.because: the model the handover writer uses
